transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Rios (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Fluxion Head of ML), Dan Becker (Fluxion Director of Platform), Sofia Martinez (Fluxion Channel Ops), Leo Grant (Fluxion CISO)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/joint-account-playbook (deck), https://sheets.google.com/fluxion-joint-mapping (spreadsheet)

Summary:
Quick partner-facing pipeline review to align on 5 pilot accounts, agree technical gating (VPC/private option vs hosted), pricing carve (channel discount thresholds), and next steps for joint exec alignment with partner OptiPartners. SE to scope perf baseline and run quick cost/latency estimate, AE to own mapping sheet and initial co-sell playbook. Security and contract items flagged for Leo and Sofia.

Topics:
- high level account list & ownership
- pilot objectives and KPIs (activation, latency, cost per 1k tokens)
- deployment options (hosted API vs Redwood Dedicated vs Private VPC)
- partner margin & channel discounts
- security controls and audit readiness
- timeline and next steps

Action items (brief in-call):
- AE to share mapping + playbook link
- SE to run perf/costs for 5 accounts
- Customer to confirm pilots + provide security wishlist

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick intro round?
[00:12] Maya: hi, maya here, head of ml at fluxion, thanks for organizing.
[00:17] Dan: dan from platform team, i'll be the technical lead on our side for pilots.
[00:22] Sofia: sofia, channel ops, i'll coordinate partner contracts and partner alignment.
[00:26] Leo: leo, ciso, i'll chime in on security constraints.
[00:30] Marco: marco, redwood se, i'll go through the perf/back-of-envelope on the model side later.
[00:34] Avery: great. objective for today: align on top pilot accounts, confirm who owns which accounts, identify any technical blockers for private deployment or dedicated capacity, and agree next steps to get a joint exec alignment meeting scheduled.
[00:50] Maya: top priority for us is time-to-prod for two product integrations — we need sub-200ms token latency ideally but more importantly predictable 99p latency and cost control.
[01:06] Dan: to add, our infra is mostly GCP with a hybrid edge pattern, some accounts require data residency in eu-west1 due to regs.
[01:18] Sofia: partners will want clear margins, we can't give too deep a discount unless there's committed reserved capacity.
[01:30] Avery: understood. one thing i wanted to confirm — are you expecting us to bring a partner, OptiPartners, into the joint account?
[01:38] Maya: yes, OptiPartners will co-sell and sometimes do implementation. Sofia, you'll coordinate?
[01:43] Sofia: yes, we'll bring them in, but we need a partner playbook and clear account mapping so there's no overlap.
[01:50] Marco: quick question on deployment: fluxion, do you expect private on-prem for the pilots or will hosted/dedicated suffice?
[01:58] Dan: for the majority, hosted is fine, but two accounts want VPC/private deployment because of IP/data residency, and one is considering on-prem later.
[02:10] Marco: ok, good to know. that affects perf numbers and kernel selection — quantization profiles do better in dedicated/dedicated-quantized setups.
[02:22] Avery: i'm going to share the joint-account sheet after this call, it has columns for owner, partner involvement, required deployment mode, timeline, and success metrics.
[02:33] Maya: perfect.
[02:36] Leo: security: before we sign anything we need SAML SSO, audit logs retention 12 months, and KMS/HSM integration for key management. can you support HSM import?
[02:49] Marco: we support KMS integrations; HSM import is possible with the private deployment path. on hosted we do envelope encryption, and we can show audit log hooks to your SIEM.
[03:02] Leo: also need SOC2 type 2 evidence and an ISO statement.
[03:07] Avery: we have SOC2 and ISO bits in our security pack — i'll drop the security folder with specific docs.
[03:13] Sofia: would be helpful to get a one pager of controls so i can send to procurement.
[03:18] Avery: noted, will send.
[03:20] Marco: technical blocker note: if you want VPC/private we usually do a minimal validation benchmark — we'll need a sample request distribution, small prompt sets, and expected concurrency.
[03:33] Dan: we can provide that. our expected peak is ~50 requests per second across two endpoints during pilot spikes, avg 20 req/s.
[03:42] Marco: great, i'll run a baseline and give latency and cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated vs private. i'll call out token cost and effective per-1k-token pricing variance.
[03:54] Maya: about the model — are we locked to a specific open model? we prefer a family that supports instruction tuning and custom safety layers.
[04:03] Marco: we can host multiple variants. for production you might start with a 7B quantized variant for cost then upgrade to 13B or 70B for quality where needed; also we have model fallback routing to keep latency SLOs during capacity spikes.
[04:20] Maya: fallback sounds good. are fallbacks automatic or manual?
[04:23] Avery: routing policies can be automatic by latency or capacity thresholds, and you can pin accounts to versions if you want deterministic outputs during evaluation windows.
[04:33] Sofia: back to partner margins — if optipartners introduces implementation services, what's typical channel discount to allow them 20% margin?
[04:44] Avery: we generally give tiered discounts based on reserved capacity. for a 12-month reserved commit we can look at up to 18% off list for the partner, but exact numbers depend on seat counts and token volumes.
[04:59] Sofia: ok that'll likely work if we can guarantee a minimum.
[05:02] Dan: any performance guarantees? we need a SLA for 95th vs 99th p99 numbers during pilot.
[05:09] Avery: for dedicated we can commit latency SLOs in the contract; for hosted we publish profiles but SLA is more conservative. can capture in canary SLA docs.
[05:20] Leo: audit trails: will we get token-level tracing to investigate customer incidents?
[05:26] Marco: yes, we can surface token-level traces and per-route logs to your observability stack, but PII redaction needs to be configured.
[05:35] Maya: speaking of PII, how does Redwood handle prompt caching and prefix caching? we don't want customer prompts accidentally cached across tenants.
[05:44] Marco: by default caching is per-tenant; shared prefix caches are opt-in and reserved for certain workloads. we'll surface the caching policy.
[05:52] Avery: quick check on timeline: you said pilots need to start early july?
[05:56] Maya: yes, ideal pilot start is July 6 to align with our quarterly demo for execs.
[06:03] Avery: that gives us two and a half weeks — tight but doable if we move fast on mapping and perf. marco, can you get estimates by next week?
[06:11] Marco: yes i'll aim for June 24 with a short doc comparing hosted vs dedicated vs private for each account.
[06:18] Dan: good. on contract side, we'll need partner carve and reseller contract: sofia will coordinate with your legal.
[06:25] Sofia: i'll work with your legal — we'll need standard MSAs and SOW templates.
[06:30] Avery: i'll send the playbook and mapping sheet after the call — link will include suggested success metrics (activation rate, first-week retention, mean latency, cost per 1k tokens).
[06:41] Maya: on metrics — activation rate baseline is 12% and we want to hit 30% during pilot to decide to expand.
[06:47] Marco: i'll include example dashboards and tracing hooks you can plug into your prometheus/grafana.
[06:55] Leo: on security checklist — i need to know encryption at rest specifics and key rotation cadence.
[06:59] Marco: rotation is supported via KMS and we can do 90-day recommended cadence, longer if required by policy.
[07:07] Avery: are there any competitive constraints? i know you evaluated BigCloudAI and Inferna earlier.
[07:12] Maya: yes we did a bake-off — inferna was cheaper but had worse tail latency; bigcloud had good enterprise integrations but pricing was opaque.
[07:21] Avery: good to know. we'll emphasize transparent unit economics and the model fallback reliability.
[07:28] Dan: can you run a quick example cost calc for a typical monthly usage pattern? say 10M tokens, split 70/30 prompt/response.
[07:36] Marco: i'll produce a per-1k token cost table and overall monthly cost for 10M tokens across the three deployment modes.
[07:43] Sofia: also include partner margin carve in that spreadsheet so i can model economics for optipartners.
[07:49] Avery: yup.
[07:51] Maya: any red flags on the private deployment timeline? we have one account that needs on-prem by september.
[07:58] Marco: on-prem is heavier — requires infra onboarding and security review, usually 6–10 weeks. if September is needed, we should start validation in July.
[08:09] Dan: ok we'll prioritize the two hosted/dedicated pilots for July and keep on-prem as a parallel track.
[08:16] Avery: to close out, let's recap next steps.
[08:20] Marco: SE to run perf/cost by June 24 — baseline + decision matrix.
[08:24] Avery: AE to share mapping sheet and partner playbook by June 18.
[08:28] Maya: we'll confirm top 5 pilot accounts and metrics by June 19.
[08:32] Sofia: i'll share partner contract template and margin thresholds by June 21.
[08:36] Leo: i'll send security wishlist / must-haves by June 22.
[08:40] Avery: perfect. i'll set up the exec alignment meeting with OptiPartners for the week of June 29 — propose a 30-minute slot.
[08:46] Maya: that works.
[08:48] Dan: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[08:50] Marco: one more thing — i'll include the perf runbook with a small script you can run to collect sample traffic. will send with the estimate.
[08:58] Avery: great. thanks all. we'll follow up via the mapping sheet and the security packet.
[09:04] (crosstalk) Sofia: thanks, bye.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings — VPC was transcribed in places as 'V-P-C', KV cache sometimes as 'K-V cache'. Proper nouns may be off in automated captioning.
